note: Pravara is derived from gotra, never stored independently. Add new gotras here; aliases are matched after normalising case, spaces, punctuation and a trailing 'gotra'.
disclaimer: Traditional lineage information. Pronunciation, spelling and customs vary by region and family.

vedic_roots.title: Vedic roots
vedic_roots.text: The family's gotra and pravara lineage, together with birth details used in Vedic astrology. These are traditional identifiers, not genetic or legal records.

gotra.title: Gotra
gotra.text: A patrilineal clan or lineage, traditionally traced to a founding rishi. Gotra is used in ritual identification and in marriage rules that prohibit marrying within the same gotra.

pravara.title: Pravara
pravara.text: The set of illustrious rishis in a gotra lineage, recited during rituals and used alongside gotra in marriage matching. The list and its order are fixed by lineage.

rishi.title: Rishi
rishi.text: A Vedic seer or sage. A pravara names the ancestral rishis associated with the lineage.

tryarsheya.title: Tryarsheya
tryarsheya.text: A pravara made up of three rishis (tri + arsheya). It is the most common form of pravara.

pancharsheya.title: Pancharsheya
pancharsheya.text: A pravara made up of five rishis (pancha + arsheya).

rashi.title: Rashi
rashi.text: The moon sign (janma rashi): the zodiac sign the Moon occupied at the time of birth in Vedic astrology.

nakshatra.title: Nakshatra
nakshatra.text: A lunar mansion, one of the 27 divisions of the zodiac used in Vedic astrology. The birth nakshatra is used in naming and in marriage matching.

birth_time.title: Birth time
birth_time.text: The time of birth used, together with the date and place, to cast a Vedic birth chart.

birth_place.title: Vedic birth place
birth_place.text: The place of birth used to fix the local horizon when casting a Vedic birth chart.

chart_url.title: Birth chart
chart_url.text: A link to the person's kundali or birth chart, if one has been prepared.

notes.title: Notes
notes.text: Additional Vedic or family-lineage notes recorded for this person.

veda.title: Veda
veda.text: The Veda followed by the family: Rig, Yajur, Sama or Atharva. It shapes the ritual tradition and the texts used in ceremonies.

shakha.title: Shakha
shakha.text: A branch or recension of a Veda. Families often preserve a particular shakha and its recitation style.

sutra.title: Sutra
sutra.text: The ritual or household sutra followed by the family, such as Apastamba, Bodhayana or Ashvalayana. It guides domestic ceremonies.

purvikam.title: Purvikam
purvikam.text: The ancestral or family tradition recorded for this person, where the sheet provides it.

kula_devatha.title: Kula Devatha
kula_devatha.text: The family deity (kula devata) worshipped by the lineage.

parvata.title: Parvata
parvata.text: The family or lineage mountain, where the sheet records one.

sampradaya.title: Sampradaya
sampradaya.text: A spiritual lineage or tradition within Vaishnavism. For Sri Vaishnavas (Iyengars), the main sampradayas are Vadakalai and Thenkalai, differing in philosophy, rituals, and sacred marks.

acharya_thirumaligai.title: Acharya Thirumaligai
acharya_thirumaligai.text: The hereditary spiritual preceptor's lineage (matham or pontiff seat) to which a Sri Vaishnava family belongs. The Acharya provides spiritual guidance, initiates disciples, and performs key religious ceremonies.

pada.title: Pada
pada.text: A quarter of a nakshatra. Each of the 27 nakshatras spans 13°20' of the zodiac and is divided into four padas of 3°20' each. The pada of the birth Moon refines the nakshatra reading and is used in naming syllables.

lagna.title: Lagna
lagna.text: The ascendant: the rasi rising on the eastern horizon at the moment and place of birth. It anchors the South Indian chart and changes roughly every two hours, which is why an accurate birth time matters.

jadagam.title: Jadagam
jadagam.text: The Vedic birth chart (janma kundali). In the South Indian style the twelve rasis are fixed in a square grid and the grahas are placed in the rasis they occupied at birth; the lagna box carries the ascendant mark. Positions are sidereal (Lahiri ayanamsa), computed with Swiss Ephemeris.

bharadwaja.about: Named after Rishi Bharadwaja, a Saptarishi of the Angirasa lineage. The pravara invokes Angirasa, Barhaspatya and Bharadwaja.

kashyapa.about: Named after Rishi Kashyapa, a Saptarishi. The pravara invokes Kashyapa, Avatsara and Naidhruva.

srivatsa.about: A Bhargava-lineage gotra. Its five-rishi pravara invokes Bhargava, Chyavana, Apnavana, Aurva and Jamadagnya.

harita.about: Named after Harita. The most widely used pravara invokes Angirasa, Ambarisha and Yuvanasva; some families recite Harita, Ambarisha and Yuvanasva instead.
